extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners in bacteriology/microbiology laboratory practicals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural laboratory manual guidance for preparing, fixing, staining, mounting, and microscopically examining bacteria and micro‑fungi (living and killed specimens), including required apparatus, reagents, and illumination techniques. Emphasises aseptic technique, choice/preparation of stains and fixatives, and microscope setup for brightfield and dark‑ground methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement with stage micrometer
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the number of complete revolutions (by means of the recording comb) and the fractions of a revolution (by means of scale on the head of the micrometer screw), which are required to measure the 0.01 mm. Make several such estimations and average the results. Note the optical combination employed in this experiment and record it carefully, together with the micrometer value in terms of mu. Repeat this process for each of the different optical combinations and record the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To measure an object, note the number of revolutions and fractions of a revolution required to traverse the object from edge to edge, and express the result as micra by reference to the recorded values for that particular optical combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and preparation of microscope illuminant
rubrics_metrics.description: In tropical and subtropical regions diffuse daylight is the best illuminant. In temperate climes daylight of the desirable quantity is not always available, and oil lamps, gas lamps (preferably with incandescent mantles), and electricity may be used; electricity is the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple laboratory electric lamp holder (base board weighted with lead, lamp holder, curved sheet‑iron reflector) is described. An obscured metal filament lamp ~16 candle power is most suitable. For monochromatic (blue) light, streak a blue grease pencil on the lamp glass nearest the microscope and rub to an even film when warm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential apparatus and reagents for routine microscopical examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each student should be provided with specified apparatus and reagents for routine work: india‑rubber change‑mat; squares of blotting paper (German lined preferred); 2% lysol jars for infected cover‑glasses/pipettes; glazed earthenware disinfectant box with perforated lining; Bunsen burner with 'peep‑flame' by‑pass; porcelain trough for hanging‑drop slides; hanging‑drop slides (Boettcher modification) or ring cells; aluminium rods with platino‑iridium wires (loop, spatula, needle) for inoculating; two pairs of sharp spring forceps (one reserved for clean cover‑slips); box of clean 3×1 glass slips; glass capsule of cover‑slips in absolute alcohol; grease pencil; wooden staining rack with specified drop‑bottles/reagents; Canada balsam pot and sterile vaseline pots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific reagents in the rack (aniline water; gentian violet sat. alcoholic; Lugol's iodine; absolute alcohol; methylene‑blue; carbolic acid 5%; acetic acid 1%; sulphuric acid 25%; xylol; etc.) and recommends manufacturers for stains (Gruebler or Merck).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred hanging‑drop slide form and anti‑pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Best form of hanging‑drop slide is a modification of Boettcher's glass ring slide prepared by cementing a circular tin cell (13–15 mm diam., 1–2 mm high) to a 3×1 slip; sometimes two cells on one slide are convenient. Another form (ground concavity/cell) is more expensive, less convenient, easily contaminated and should be carefully avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains convenience and contamination risk; illustration referenced (Fig. 62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and mounting of platinum inoculating wires
rubrics_metrics.description: Three aluminium rods (~25 cm) carrying 0.015 gauge platino‑iridium wire 7.5 cm long: one end bent into an oval loop ('loop' or 'oese'), one flattened to form a 'spatula', one pointed as a needle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed method for mounting the platinum wire into aluminium handles: drill hole, sink channel, pass wire, bend and press into cuts, close with light hammer taps. Notes that fusing wire into glass handle is inferior to aluminium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aseptic technique for opening/closing culture tubes and sterilising loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Flame the cotton‑wool plug, extinguish flame while rotating tube; hold tube near centre with mouth upward and nearly horizontal to reduce contamination; sterilise platinum loop in Bunsen flame until red hot and sterilise aluminium handle by quick passes through flame; cool loop before use by touching condensation water or avoiding contact with medium; never allow sterilised loop to touch anything until used; replace plug with 'screwing' motion and return tube to rack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise technique (steps 2–9) emphasises flame sterilisation, proper hand positions, avoiding contamination, and re‑sterilisation after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of fresh (living, unstained) slide specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean and dry a 3×1 slip, place on filter paper; deposit a drop of distilled water (or 1% caustic potash) on centre with platinum loop; remove material from culture with sterile loop and mix with the drop; sterilise loop after use; flame cover‑slip, lower onto drop carefully to avoid air bubbles, then examine microscopically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During examination stains/reagents may be run in under a cover‑slip by placing drop at one edge and drawing blotting paper at the opposite side to draw reagent across the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative stain (Burri) method for demonstrating bacteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reagent: liquid waterproof black drawing ink 25 c.c. + tincture of iodine 1 c.c., stand 24 hours, centrifugalise, pipette supernatant, add thymol crystal or one drop formalin as preservative. Method: deposit drop of ink and a drop of culture, mix, place second slide at ~60°, draw across to spread, discard second slide into disinfectant, air‑dry first slide, add immersion oil and examine with 1/12‑inch objective without cover‑slip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Film may be permanently mounted with long cover‑glass and xylol balsam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanging‑drop preparation method and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Smear sterile vaseline on ring cell, flame cover‑slip, place drop of water on cover‑slip, obtain material and mix with drop, invert cover‑slip onto ring so drop is centred, avoid contact between drop and ring or vaseline (if contact, discard into lysol and remake), press cover‑slip into vaseline to seal and retard evaporation, then examine microscopically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cover‑slip contacts ring or vaseline and becomes infected, drop into disinfectant and make a new preparation; cover‑slip only is infected in hanging‑drop and may be removed with forceps into disinfectant when finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations to record from fresh/hanging‑drop specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine: (1) nature of bacteria present (cocci, bacilli, etc.); (2) purity of the cultivation (only when gross morphological differences exist); (3) presence or absence of spores; (4) presence or absence and character of mobility (Brownian, streaming, true locomotive motility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines Brownian movement (vibratory, relative positions unchanged), streaming (currents due to jarring/evaporation/tilt, relative positions may vary), and locomotive movement (individual bacillus changes position independently). Mobility character must be carefully determined by noting relative positions of adjacent organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent staining of hanging‑drop specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove cover‑slip with forceps; if drop small, fix face downward on Gulland's or corrosive sublimate solution; if large, place face upward and allow to dry then fix in alcohol/ether; dip cover‑glass in hot water to remove vaseline, wash in alcohol, xylol, ether, alcohol to remove grease, wash in water, stain, wash, dry and mount as ordinary cover‑slip film preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides stepwise method for converting hanging‑drop to permanent mount (vide pages referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Killed, stained method: preparing, fixing, staining, mounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Three distinct processes: preparing and fixing the film, staining, mounting. Preparing: flame cover‑slip, place drop of water, mix with material, spread evenly in square film to within 1 mm of edges, air dry. Fixing: pass cover‑slip three or four times through Bunsen flame or fix by uniform 115°C for 20 minutes in regulated oven; fixation may also be by immersion in specified fixative fluids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists alternative fixatives and conditions (see next metric): fixation coagulates albuminous material and ensures adhesion of film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved fixatives and fixation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Several fixative methods given: (1) Absolute alcohol for 5–15 minutes; (2) Absolute alcohol + Ether equal parts for 5–30 minutes (e.g., for blood or milk); (3) Osmic acid 1% aqueous for 30 seconds; (4) Corrosive sublimate (saturated aqueous) for 5 minutes; (5) Corrosive sublimate (Lang) formula and 5 minutes; (6) Gulland's solution (alcohol+ether+corrosive sublimate) for 5 minutes; (7) Formalin 10% aqueous (=4% formaldehyde)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that fixation coagulates albuminous material and ensures perfect adhesion; for micrometric observations uniform oven fixation at 115°C for 20 minutes is almost essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearing procedures and pre‑stain treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: After fixation wash cover‑slip thoroughly in running water and proceed to staining. If film from broth/gelatine/pus/morbid exudations, saturate film with 2% acetic acid for two minutes then wash with alcohol to 'clear' groundwork. If film from blood or bloodstained fluid, treat with 2% acetic acid for two minutes after fixation, wash with water, dry, then stain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearing improves sharpness and cleanliness of film; washing and alcohol treatments must be performed gently when delicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staining principles: dyes, penetration enhancers and common aniline dyes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover film with selected stain for a few minutes then wash off excess. Penetrating power of stains increased by (a) heating; (b) chemical means — addition of carbolic acid 5% aqueous, caustic alkalies 2% aqueous, water saturated with aniline oil, borax 0.5% aqueous. Common aniline basic dyes: methylene‑blue, gentian violet, fuchsin (kept in saturated alcoholic solutions). Carbolic methylene‑blue and carbol fuchsin prepared by covering film with 5% carbolic acid then adding saturated alcoholic dye; aniline gentian violet prepared by adding dye to saturated aniline oil in water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives recipes and proportions for saturated aqueous/alcoholic solutions and for carbolic/alkaline variants (see stock stains metric). Notes that basic dyes are kept saturated alcoholic to retard decomposition; two or three drops of alcoholic dye to ~4 c.c. water commonly used for cover‑slip film preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decolourisation hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: After overstaining, films may be decolourised by washing in reagents arranged in ascending order of power: (1) Water; (2) Chloroform; (3) Acetic acid 1%; (4) Alcohol; (5) Alcohol absolute + Acetic acid 1% (equal parts); (6) Mineral acids (hydrochloric 1% aqueous or alcoholic 90% solution; sulphuric 25% aqueous; nitric 33% aqueous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose decolourising reagent appropriate to degree of overstaining; stronger reagents progressively remove more stain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterstaining: choice of contrasting dyes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use colours which will contrast with the first stain. Examples: Vesuvin, Neutral red, Eosin for films stained by methylene‑blue or Gram's method; Fuchsin, Methylene‑blue, Gentian violet for films stained by fuchsin; Methylene‑blue, Gentian violet for films stained by fuchsin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select counterstain to produce clear contrast with primary stain; examples given for common pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mounting permanent preparations
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash film carefully in running water, blot off superfluous water with filter paper, complete drying in air or by holding cover‑slip above Bunsen flame, place a drop of xylol balsam on centre of clean 3×1 slide and invert cover‑slip over balsam, lowering carefully to avoid air bubbles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: xylol preferred to chloroform to dissolve Canada balsam because xylol does not decolourise the specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of impression films (Klatschpräparat) from plate colonies
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove clean cover‑slip, burn off spirit, open plate and rest one edge of cover‑slip on medium beside selected colony, lower horizontally without lateral movement, apply gentle vertical pressure with forceps to ensure contact, raise cover‑slip using needle under opposite edge so colony adheres, place cover‑slip film uppermost on rubber mat, cover with inverted watch‑glass until dry, fix in fixing fluid, clear with acetic acid and alcohol, stain and mount as ordinary film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform all washing operations with extreme gentleness to preserve film characteristics used to examine colony formation under higher powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical examination procedure for unstained specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Place body tube vertical, arrange hanging‑drop on stage so drop is in optical axis and secure with clips, use 1/6‑inch objective, rack down body tube until front lens almost contacts cover‑slip (within focal distance), apply eye and adjust plane mirror for best illumination, rack condenser down slightly and reduce iris aperture so light is even and dim, then rack up body tube with coarse adjustment until organisms come into view and focus with fine adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If difficulty finding hanging‑drop don't rack body tube down with eye at ocular (risk of forcing front lens through cover‑glass and contaminating objective); withdraw eye, rack tube up and recommence from step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark‑ground illumination setup and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Set microscope vertical and insert highest eyepiece; use 2/3‑inch objective (then later replace with 1/12‑inch oil immersion with special stop), remove substage condenser and fit dark‑ground condenser; place illuminant 30–50 cm from microscope (Liliput Arc Lamp, Nernst Lamp or incandescent gas lamp with bull's‑eye condenser for parallel rays), centre concentric rings on condenser with centring screws, prepare fresh specimen on thin slips (<1 mm) and No.1 cover‑glasses (0.17 mm) cleaned with soft washleather (not emery paper), deposit large drop of immersion oil on condenser, rack down condenser to contact slide, adjust mirror to produce bright spot, replace 2/3‑inch objective with 1/12‑inch oil immersion lens fitted with special stop, place immersion oil on cover‑glass and lower tube until front lens enters oil, focus bright spot and adjust condenser height until best position found so bacteria stand out bright against dark background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scratches on slides (produce haziness); use immersion oil or pure water on condenser; ensure centring and adjustment of mirror and condenser for optimal dark‑ground contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical examination of stained specimens (oil immersion brightfield)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure slide with spring clips, place a drop of cedarwood (immersion) oil on centre of cover‑slip, use 1/12‑inch oil immersion lens, rack down body tube until front lens contacts oil and nearly touches cover‑slip, rack up condenser into contact with under surface of slide, adjust plane mirror for maximum light, rack up body tube until stained film comes into view, focus condenser and then focus film accurately with fine adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description of cedarwood oil bottle design (inverted cone cavity, safety funnel, dust cap with wooden rod) for safe application of oil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock stains and their preparation (methylene‑blue, gentian violet, thionine, fuchsin, contrast and tissue stains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recipes and preparation methods for a range of stains: methylene‑blue (saturated aqueous, saturated alcoholic, carbolic methylene‑blue, alkaline Loeffler preparation), gentian violet (saturated aqueous/alcoholic, carbolic gentian violet, anilin water solution), thionine blue (carbolic), fuchsin (saturated aqueous/alcoholic, carbolic Ziehl), contrast stains (eosin aqueous/alcoholic, safranine aqueous, neutral red), vesuvin (Bismarck brown), tissue stains (aniline gentian violet for Weigert's fibrin stain, haematoxylin Ehrlich and Mayer's haematin) with ingredient weights and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on preparation times (e.g., methylene‑blue in water two weeks shaking daily), storage/ preservatives (e.g., add thymol or one drop formalin), dilution instructions before use, and that certain preparations will not keep longer than specified (e.g., anilin gentian solution ~14 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability note on methods printed in ordinary vs small type
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods printed in ordinary type are those which long experience has shown to be the most reliable and to give the best results; those relegated to small type comprise methods not so generally useful but which give excellent results in the hands of the experienced worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ordinary‑type methods as default for routine work; reserve small‑type methods for experienced operators.
